intro: Pandas NumPy ke upar labelled data deta hai: rows, columns, index aur missing values. Is section me Series/DataFrame banana, filter, groupby, merge, sort aur pivot tak ka practical workflow cover hota hai — wahi 80% jo daily analysis me chahiye.
theory: Series ek labelled 1-D array hai; DataFrame labelled columns ka collection. Har column ka apna dtype hota hai.
Selection ka rule: `df["col"]` column deta hai, `df[["a", "b"]]` frame, `df.loc[row_label, col_label]` label se, `df.iloc[i, j]` position se.
Boolean mask se filter hota hai; multiple conditions ko parentheses me `&`/`|` se jodo. `query()` readable alternative hai.
groupby split-apply-combine karta hai: group banao, aggregate/transform karo, result combine karo. `agg` multiple metrics ek saath deta hai.
merge join keys par tables jodta hai; validate= fan-out pakadta hai. Missing values ke liye isna/fillna/dropna, reshape ke liye pivot_table/melt.
syntax:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["pune", "delhi"], "sales": [100, 250]})
print(df["sales"].mean())
print(df[df["sales"] > 150])

summary = df.groupby("city")["sales"].sum()
wide = df.pivot_table(index="city", values="sales", aggfunc="sum")
joined = left.merge(right, on="id", how="left", validate="many_to_one")

df.sort_values("sales", ascending=False)
df.assign(margin=lambda d: d["sales"] - d["cost"])
df["price"].fillna(df["price"].median())

Output ko print se verify karo.
Ye Pandas for Data Science ka basic building block hai.

Ek step aur jodne se behaviour kaise badalta hai, dekho.
Input badal kar edge case test karo.

Output ko project/interview me evidence ki tarah use karo.

realWorld: Sales/ops reports me groupby + pivot_table se city/product wise totals nikalte hain aur missing values ko median se bharte hain.
Do exports (orders aur customers) ko merge karke unmatched rows ka indicator se pata lagaya jata hai.
Time series me resample/rolling se weekly totals aur moving averages banti hain — pandas ka core analytics use case.

interview.q: loc aur iloc me fark batao.
interview.a: loc label-based hai (index/column names), iloc integer position-based. Slice semantics bhi alag hain: loc ka end label include hota hai, iloc ka end position exclude.

interview.q: SettingWithCopyWarning kyun aata hai?
interview.a: Jab aap slice ki copy par assign karte hain aur pandas ko clear nahi hota ki original badalna hai ya copy. Fix: ek step me `.loc[mask, "col"] = value` likho ya `.copy()` explicit karo.

interview.q: merge validate kya karta hai?
interview.a: Expected cardinality (one_to_one, one_to_many, many_to_one, many_to_many) check karta hai aur fan-out par MergeError deta hai — silent row multiplication se bachata hai.

interview.q: groupby ke baad transform aur agg me kya antar hai?
interview.a: agg group ko ek row me collapse karta hai; transform har original row ke liye group-level value deta hai, isliye row count same rehta hai.

debugging.error: Logic error — pehla do items chahiye the, sirf pehla aaya
debugging.why: Slice ka end exclusive hota hai; 0:1 sirf index 0 deta hai. Ye Pandas for Data Science ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.lesson: Slice boundaries exclusive hoti hain — range jaisa hi rule.

debugging.error: TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str
debugging.why: String concatenation ko dono taraf str chahiye; Python implicit conversion nahi karta. Ye Pandas for Data Science ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: f-string ya str() se explicit conversion karo.
debugging.lesson: TypeError type mismatch batata hai — conversion explicit karo.

debugging.error: IndexError: list index out of range
debugging.why: List me sirf 0 aur 1 index hain; 5 par kuch nahi. Ye Pandas for Data Science ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: Index se pehle length check karo ya safe getter use karo.
debugging.correct:
scores = [10, 20]
print(scores[1] if len(scores) > 1 else None)
debugging.lesson: IndexError off-by-one aur empty collection ka signal hai.

debugging.why: Dict me score key exist nahi karti; [] missing key par KeyError deta hai. Ye Pandas for Data Science ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: get() se default do ya key ki presence check karo.
debugging.lesson: KeyError expected-missing field ka case hai — get/default se handle karo.
